text: Retrieve applicable positive and negative evidence. Keep failed approaches, applicability limits and direct evidence references. Distinguish observed results from hypotheses. Prefer error avoidance, detection and recovery before speed.
Confirm the Ascend target, runtime, source revisions and healthy available resources. Stop on mismatches before execution; retain the fault and recovery evidence.
Freeze the original goal, inputs, correctness cases and independent verifier. Separate original projects from diagnostics and retries.
Read positive and negative KDB evidence. Reflect on previous attempts before selecting a design; explain known failure avoidance and recovery before performance choices.
Implement the verified design in the task source. Preserve frozen verifiers and negative lessons. Keep changes small enough to diagnose.
Run the frozen correctness cases. Record failures and source identity before changing code. Passing a partial case set does not establish correctness.
Identify the observed failing behavior and evidence. Recover with a bounded source change, then rerun the failed cases and regression verifier.
Retrieve positive and negative evidence and reflect on previous iterations. Preserve correctness while measuring performance on the required target; retain unsuccessful optimisations.
Run the independent frozen verifier against the current source. Keep raw results and source identity. A failure returns to design or implementation.
Accept only with a passing frozen verifier on unchanged current source. Retain raw provider, SFT, KDB retrieval and skill-read evidence, including failures.
